faq: What kinds of workflows can you build?
Purchase requests, leave requests, onboarding checklists, content approvals, expense claims, change requests and similar. If work moves from person to person with a yes or no along the way, it fits.
Can people approve from their phone?
Yes. Approvers can act from the email link or the mobile view of the app, without installing anything. We test the approval step on a phone before handover.
Can it replace our spreadsheet tracker?
Yes. We can import the current tracker so open items carry over. The old sheet can stay as a read-only record until you are comfortable switching.
What if rules differ by department?
Standard adds rules by amount or department. For more complex rules, such as routing by region and amount together, Premium supports conditional steps. We confirm what is needed before building.

desc:
A workflow app for approvals and tasks routes each request to the right person, tracks its status and chases late items. Ecom Swift LLC maps one of your workflows and builds it as a web app, so people stop chasing each other by email.

## What is a workflow app?

A workflow app is a web application that moves a piece of work through a series of steps. Someone submits a form, the system sends it to an approver, the approver accepts or sends it back and the outcome is recorded. Everyone involved can see where the request stands at any time.

Common examples are purchase requests, leave requests, new hire onboarding, content approvals and expense claims. Any process that follows the same steps each time is a good candidate.

## Why approvals get stuck

When approvals live in email, no one has the full picture. The request sits in someone's inbox, the approver does not know it is urgent and the requester has no way to check. People ask in chat, forward messages and keep their own trackers. Rules such as spending limits are applied from memory and differ from person to person.

The result is delays, duplicated effort and no reliable record of who agreed to what. When something goes wrong, nobody can reconstruct the decision.

## How a workflow app affects your results

A defined process speeds up the work that waits on people. The approver gets a clear request with all the details, so decisions come faster. Reminder emails catch late items before they become a problem. A history log gives managers a clear record for audits or disputes.

The gains are in time, consistency and visibility. You spend less effort asking for updates, and requesters know where they stand. How much faster things move depends on how many handoffs the process has today and how willing your team is to use the new route.

## What a great workflow app includes

- A request form with only the fields that approvers need.
- Required fields and checks, so incomplete requests never enter the flow.
- Approval steps that route to the right person, with comments on approve or return.
- Rules that change the route, such as by amount or department.
- Parallel and conditional approvals for more complex processes.
- A status list showing every request and who it is waiting on.
- Reminder emails for items that sit too long.
- A history log for each request, recording who did what and when.
- File attachments on requests where supporting documents matter.
- Notifications in email, or in Slack or Teams for larger builds.
- A dashboard of open and late items for managers.

## What we do

We sit down with you to map the workflow as it runs today, including the exceptions that cause trouble. We then agree a cleaner version, design the form and the steps and build them. Before launch we test with real examples and walk your team through using it.

The Basic package builds one workflow with a request form, one approval step, an email to the approver and a status list. Standard adds more workflows and approval steps, rules by amount or department, reminder emails and a history log per request. Premium adds more workflows, parallel and conditional approvals, a dashboard, Slack or Teams notifications, file attachments and a staff training call. Add-ons include an extra workflow, a calendar view and PDF export.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Start with the one process that causes the most chasing.
- Write down who approves what and under which conditions.
- Name a backup approver for holidays and absences.
- Keep the form short and ask for attachments only when needed.
- Tell staff clearly when the old method stops.

**Avoid:**
- Adding approval steps that do not change a decision.
- Building every department rule into the first version.
- Sending reminders so often that people ignore them.
- Leaving requests with no owner after a rejection.
- Running the old email route and the new app side by side for long.

## Who it is for

This service suits an office manager handling purchase or leave requests by email, a marketing team that needs content approvals in order, and an operations lead who wants consistent onboarding steps for every new hire or client. It also suits a company with a spreadsheet tracker that no one fully trusts.

## What we need from you

Send a description or diagram of the current process, a copy of the form or sheet you use and a list of who approves what. Tell us which chat tool you use, if any. We never ask for passwords. Access to your tools is given as a collaborator, team or developer user, and you decide when it ends.
